contentBlocks.text: A formal essay is built on one sentence that everything else supports: the thesis statement. This week, you'll write a complete, multi-paragraph essay, starting with its foundation.

A thesis statement is a specific, arguable claim that previews what your entire essay will prove — more ambitious than a single-paragraph claim, since it has to hold up an entire multi-paragraph argument. A weak thesis is too broad: 'Social media has good and bad effects.' A strong thesis is specific and takes a real position: 'Schools should limit students' social media use during class hours because it measurably reduces both focus and in-person social skills.' Notice the strong version previews the REASONS the essay will cover. Write a thesis statement on a topic you care about, making sure it's specific enough that someone could reasonably disagree with it.
You just wrote a real thesis statement — the foundation your entire essay will be built on this week. Tomorrow we'll build the body paragraphs that prove it.

objectives: Define a thesis statement as a specific, arguable claim previewing an entire essay's argument
Write a thesis statement specific enough to support a full multi-paragraph essay
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce the thesis statement as the essay's foundation.
2. Compare the weak vs. strong social-media thesis examples.
3. Brainstorm topics the child genuinely cares about before writing.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: building body paragraphs.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide a thesis template ('[Position] because [reason 1] and [reason 2]') to fill in
Ready for more: ask them to write two different theses on the same topic and explain which one previews a stronger essay
This week's essay will be built entirely on today's thesis — encourage genuine topic investment since it carries through all 5 days
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary based on the child's chosen topic — check that the thesis is specific (not vague), takes a real position, and previews at least one or two reasons the essay will cover.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Addresses Common Core Grade 8 Writing standard W.8.1a (introduce claim(s), acknowledge alternate/opposing claims), building beyond Grade 5's single-paragraph claim toward a genuine essay-level thesis.

generationData.instructions: Write a specific, arguable thesis statement for your essay topic.
